formulas.title: Fluid Kinetic Helicity Density
formulas.description: Defines the local kinetic helicity density $H_k$ as the inner product of fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ and vorticity $\nabla \times \mathbf{u}$, measuring the corkscrew-like handedness of three-dimensional flow.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Pseudoscalar topological invariant of ideal barotropic fluid motion that quantifies the alignment between translation and spin of fluid parcels, directly powering the mean-field $\alpha$-effect in rotating dynamos.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Kinetic helicity measures how strongly a swirling fluid moves like a corkscrew—positive for right-handed spiral motion and negative for left-handed spiral motion.
formulas.interpretation: In a rapidly rotating spherical shell, Coriolis deflection correlates axial convergence with cyclonic vorticity so $H_k$ is predominantly negative in the northern hemisphere and positive in the southern hemisphere, supplying the parity-breaking source $\alpha \approx -(\tau_c/3)\langle H_k \rangle$ for large-scale dipole generation.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Transforms as a pseudoscalar under spatial inversion ($\mathbf{x} \to -\mathbf{x}$), reversing sign under mirror reflection while its volume integral is conserved in inviscid barotropic Euler flows (Moffatt's topological linkage theorem).
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes identically in strictly two-dimensional planar flows where vorticity is perpendicular to velocity. In real planetary cores, viscosity, buoyancy torque, and Lorentz forces continuously generate and dissipate local kinetic helicity.

H_k.name: Kinetic Helicity Density
H_k.description: Local scalar measure of corkscrew alignment between fluid velocity and vorticity.

\\mathbf{u}.name: Fluid Velocity Field
\\mathbf{u}.description: Three-dimensional velocity vector of the convecting fluid.

formulas.title: Elsasser Number for Lorentz-Coriolis Force Balance
formulas.description: Defines the dimensionless Elsasser number $\Lambda$ as the ratio of the Lorentz force to the Coriolis force in a rotating conducting fluid of density $\rho$, angular speed $\Omega$, magnetic diffusivity $\eta$, and magnetic flux density $B$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Key dimensionless control parameter of rotating magnetohydrodynamics distinguishing weak-field geostrophic regimes ($\Lambda \ll 1$) from strong-field magnetostrophic regimes ($\Lambda \sim 1$) where electromagnetic stresses actively reshape convection.
formulas.intuitive_summary: The Elsasser number compares the braking grip of the magnetic field against the twisting pull of planetary rotation; around unity, the two forces achieve an optimal balance for core convection.
formulas.interpretation: Estimating current density from the induced electric field $J \sim \sigma u B$ gives Lorentz force density $J B \sim \sigma u B^2 = u B^2/(\mu_0 \eta)$; dividing by the Coriolis force density $2\Omega\rho u$ cancels flow speed $u$ and yields $\Lambda = B^2/(2\Omega\rho\mu_0\eta)$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Constructed by Buckingham $\Pi$ dimensional analysis from the ratio of electromagnetic induction drag to rotating-frame inertial Coriolis acceleration.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Independent of velocity scale $u$ and length scale $L$ under the assumption $J \sim \sigma u B$ (valid at moderate magnetic Reynolds number). In Earth's outer core, internal fields of a few millitesla correspond to $\Lambda \sim 0.1$–$10$, while high-$Rm$ dynamos can exhibit scale-dependent effective Elsasser numbers.

\\Lambda.name: Elsasser Number
\\Lambda.description: Dimensionless ratio of Lorentz force to Coriolis force in a rotating conductor.

B.name: Characteristic Magnetic Flux Density
B.description: Typical internal magnetic field strength within the dynamo region.

\\Omega.name: Planetary Angular Velocity
\\Omega.description: Magnitude of the solid-body rotation rate of the planet or star.

\\rho.name: Fluid Mass Density
\\rho.description: Mean mass density of the electrically conducting fluid core.

\\mu_0.name: Vacuum Magnetic Permeability
\\mu_0.description: Fundamental permeability constant of free space ($4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ H/m).

\\eta.name: Magnetic Diffusivity
\\eta.description: Ohmic magnetic diffusivity $\eta = (\mu_0 \sigma)^{-1}$ of the fluid.

formulas.title: Magnetostrophic Rotating Momentum Balance
formulas.description: Expresses the leading-order force balance in a rapidly rotating, strongly magnetized planetary core, equating Coriolis acceleration $2\boldsymbol{\Omega} \times \mathbf{u}$ to the reduced pressure gradient, Lorentz acceleration, and buoyancy acceleration $\mathbf{g}'$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Governing asymptotic momentum equation of the MAC (Magnetic-Archimedean-Coriolis) regime in geodynamo theory, obtained by dropping small inertial and viscous accelerations from the rotating Boussinesq Navier-Stokes equation.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Deep inside Earth's fluid core, friction and inertia are so tiny at large scales that planetary rotation, pressure, magnetic tension, and buoyancy lock together in a four-way force balance.
formulas.interpretation: Taking the curl eliminates pressure and shows how magnetic stresses break the geostrophic Proudman-Taylor constraint $(\boldsymbol{\Omega}\cdot\nabla)\mathbf{u} = 0$, while integrating the azimuthal component over coaxial cylinders coaxial with $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ enforces Taylor's constraint that net cylindrical magnetic torque must vanish.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from the rotating-frame Boussinesq momentum equation in the joint asymptotic limit of vanishing Rossby number ($Ro \ll 1$) and vanishing Ekman number ($Ek \ll 1$).
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Breaks down inside thin viscous Ekman-Hartmann boundary layers near the core-mantle and inner-core boundaries, and on short timescales where inertial accelerations drive torsional Alfvén oscillations.

\\boldsymbol{\\Omega}.name: Angular Velocity Vector
\\boldsymbol{\\Omega}.description: Planetary rotation vector defining the axis of the rotating reference frame.

\\mathbf{u}.name: Fluid Velocity Field
\\mathbf{u}.description: Large-scale convective flow velocity in the rotating frame.

\\rho_0.name: Reference Fluid Density
\\rho_0.description: Boussinesq background density of the conducting liquid core.

p.name: Modified Pressure
p.description: Dynamic pressure departure from hydrostatic and centrifugal equilibrium.

\\mu_0.name: Vacuum Magnetic Permeability
\\mu_0.description: Permeability of free space coupling current density $\mu_0^{-1}\nabla \times \mathbf{B}$ to Lorentz force.

\\mathbf{B}.name: Magnetic Flux Density
\\mathbf{B}.description: Internal planetary magnetic field exerting Lorentz stresses on the flow.

\\mathbf{g}'.name: Reduced Buoyancy Acceleration
\\mathbf{g}'.description: Thermal and compositional buoyancy force per unit mass driving core convection.

formulas.title: Convective Power-Based Planetary Magnetic Field Scaling
formulas.description: Scales the saturated root-mean-square internal magnetic field $B_{\mathrm{rms}}$ of a rapidly rotating convective dynamo with mean fluid density $\rho_0$, shell thickness $L$, and specific convective buoyancy power flux $q_0$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Universal energy-flux scaling law unifying magnetic field strengths across terrestrial planets, gas giants, and fully convective stars by equating ohmic dissipation to available buoyant convective power.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A planet's or star's magnetic field strength is set primarily by how much convective heat power flows through its conducting interior, scaling as the cube root of buoyancy power.
formulas.interpretation: Because ohmic dissipation balances buoyant power injection $P \sim \rho_0 q_0$ while magnetic energy density $B_{\mathrm{rms}}^2/(2\mu_0)$ scales with convective power flux $(q_0 L)^{2/3}$ independently of rotation rate $\Omega$ and diffusivity $\eta$, taking the square root gives $B_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto (\mu_0 \rho_0)^{1/2} (q_0 L)^{1/3}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from asymptotic diffusivity-free energy balance in rapidly rotating, strongly supercritical convective dynamos where viscous losses are subdominant to ohmic dissipation.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds for dipolar, rapidly rotating convective dynamos (Earth, Jupiter, rapidly rotating M-dwarfs) where local Rossby number remains below the multipolar transition ($Ro_\ell \lesssim 0.12$). Fails for weakly supercritical, inertia-dominated, or strongly stratified multipolar dynamos.

B_{\\mathrm{rms}}.name: Root-Mean-Square Magnetic Field
B_{\\mathrm{rms}}.description: Volume-averaged root-mean-square internal magnetic flux density in the dynamo shell.

\\mu_0.name: Vacuum Magnetic Permeability
\\mu_0.description: Permeability of free space converting magnetic energy density to flux density.

\\rho_0.name: Mean Core Fluid Density
\\rho_0.description: Characteristic mass density of the convecting electrically conducting region.

q_0.name: Specific Convective Buoyancy Power
q_0.description: Convective buoyancy power per unit mass available to drive dynamo action ($\mathrm{m^2/s^3}$).

L.name: Convective Shell Thickness
L.description: Characteristic radial depth of the electrically conducting convecting shell.

formulas.title: Linear Scalar Acoustic Wave Equation
formulas.description: Governs the propagation of infinitesimal adiabatic pressure perturbations $p'$ through a homogeneous, quiescent, inviscid compressible fluid at the isentropic sound speed $c_s$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: A linear hyperbolic partial differential equation expressing the dynamic balance between fluid inertia and elastic bulk compressibility for small-amplitude sound waves.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Small pressure ripples in a fluid travel outward without changing speed or shape at the sound speed set by the medium's stiffness and density.
formulas.interpretation: Combining the linearized continuity equation $\partial \rho' / \partial t + \rho_0 \nabla \cdot \mathbf{u} = 0$, linearized Euler momentum balance $\rho_0 \partial \mathbf{u} / \partial t = -\nabla p'$, and isentropic equation of state $p' = c_s^2 \rho'$ eliminates velocity and density fluctuations to yield the d'Alembert wave equation for $p'$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Exhibits spatial translation, rotational isotropy, time-reversal invariance, and Lorentz-like acoustic boost invariance with characteristic signal speed $c_s$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid when acoustic Mach number $|u|/c_s \ll 1$, fractional density change $|\rho'|/\rho_0 \ll 1$, and thermoviscous dissipation is negligible over propagation distances of interest. High-amplitude waves require the nonlinear Westervelt equation.

p'.name: Acoustic Overpressure
p'.description: Small-amplitude pressure perturbation relative to ambient equilibrium pressure.

c_s.name: Isentropic Speed of Sound
c_s.description: Phase velocity of infinitesimal adiabatic longitudinal waves in the fluid.

formulas.title: Characteristic Specific Acoustic Impedance
formulas.description: Defines the characteristic specific acoustic impedance $Z_0$ of a homogeneous medium as the product of its ambient equilibrium mass density $\rho_0$ and isentropic sound speed $c_s$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Measures the ratio of acoustic overpressure to longitudinal particle velocity in a progressive plane sound wave, quantifying a medium's resistance to acoustic motion.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Denser, stiffer materials have higher acoustic impedance, causing sound waves to reflect strongly whenever they hit a boundary between mismatched media.
formulas.interpretation: Substituting a forward-traveling plane wave $p'(x,t) = f(x - c_s t)$ into linearized momentum conservation $\rho_0 \partial u / \partial t = -\partial p' / \partial x$ gives $p' / u = \rho_0 c_s = Z_0$, which sets normal-incidence reflection amplitude $R = (Z_2 - Z_1)/(Z_2 + Z_1)$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from one-dimensional translational invariance and linear constitutive proportionality between stress and particle velocity in progressive acoustic modes.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly real and frequency-independent only for lossless, non-dispersive plane waves in the far field. In spherical near fields or dissipative viscoelastic media, specific acoustic impedance becomes complex and frequency-dependent.

Z_0.name: Characteristic Specific Acoustic Impedance
Z_0.description: Ratio of acoustic pressure to particle velocity for a progressive plane wave (also measured in rayls).

\\rho_0.name: Ambient Mass Density
\\rho_0.description: Equilibrium mass density of the undisturbed acoustic medium.

c_s.name: Isentropic Speed of Sound
c_s.description: Linear adiabatic propagation speed of longitudinal acoustic waves.

formulas.title: Westervelt Nonlinear Acoustic Wave Equation
formulas.equation: \nabla^2 p' - \frac{1}{c_s^2}\frac{\partial^2 p'}{\partial t^2} + \frac{\delta}{c_s^4}\frac{\partial^3 p'}{\partial t^3} = -\frac{\beta}{\rho_0 c_s^4}\frac{\partial^2 (p')^2}{\partial t^2}
formulas.description: Models finite-amplitude acoustic wave propagation in a thermoviscous fluid, coupling three-dimensional diffraction and sound diffusivity $\delta$ to cumulative quadratic nonlinearity parameterized by $\beta$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Extends the linear scalar wave equation to second order in acoustic Mach number to capture harmonic generation, waveform steepening, shock formation, and parametric beam mixing.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Loud sound waves distort as their high-pressure peaks outrun their low-pressure troughs, while fluid viscosity and heat conduction smooth the resulting steep shock fronts.
formulas.interpretation: Obtained from the Kuznetsov equation by neglecting local non-cumulative Lagrangian energy density terms that vanish for progressive waves; the right-hand source scales with the nonlinearity coefficient $\beta = 1 + B/(2A)$ and drives second-harmonic and difference-frequency generation.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Preserves spatial rotational and translational invariance of the underlying compressible Navier-Stokes equations while explicitly breaking time-reversal symmetry through the odd-order diffusive derivative $\delta \partial^3 p' / \partial t^3$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for weakly nonlinear, weakly dissipative progressive waves ($|u|/c_s \ll 1$, $\omega \delta / c_s^2 \ll 1$) over propagation distances spanning many wavelengths where cumulative nonlinearity dominates local effects. Reduces to the Burgers equation for one-dimensional plane waves.

p'.name: Acoustic Pressure Perturbation
p'.description: Finite-amplitude overpressure field propagating through the fluid.

c_s.name: Small-Signal Sound Speed
c_s.description: Linear isentropic speed of sound in the quiescent medium.

\\delta.name: Diffusivity of Sound
\\delta.description: Thermoviscous attenuation coefficient combining shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, and thermal conductivity.

\\beta.name: Coefficient of Nonlinearity
\\beta.description: Dimensionless nonlinearity parameter $\beta = 1 + B/(2A)$ (equal to $(\gamma + 1)/2$ for an ideal gas).

\\rho_0.name: Ambient Fluid Density
\\rho_0.description: Equilibrium mass density of the undisturbed fluid.

formulas.title: Maxwell Linear Viscoelastic Constitutive Equation
formulas.description: Relates total uniaxial strain rate $d\varepsilon/dt$ to stress $\sigma$ and stress rate $d\sigma/dt$ in a linear viscoelastic Maxwell material with elastic Young's modulus $E$ and dynamic viscosity $\eta$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Models a viscoelastic fluid as an ideal elastic spring in series with a viscous dashpot, producing instantaneous elastic deformation followed by exponential stress relaxation under constant strain.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A Maxwell material acts like a stiff spring when struck suddenly, yet flows steadily like thick honey when held under load for a long time.
formulas.interpretation: Because the spring and dashpot share the same stress $\sigma$, their strain rates add linearly ($\dot{\varepsilon} = \dot{\varepsilon}_e + \dot{\varepsilon}_v$). Holding strain constant ($\dot{\varepsilon} = 0$) yields exponential stress relaxation $\sigma(t) = \sigma_0 \exp(-t/\tau_r)$ with relaxation time $\tau_r = \eta / E$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Constructed from linear superposition of reversible Hookean elasticity and irreversible Newtonian viscous dissipation under time-translation invariance.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Captures stress relaxation accurately for dilute polymer solutions and viscoelastic liquids at small strains, but predicts unbounded linear creep under constant stress and neglects multi-mode relaxation spectra; large finite deformations require upper-convected Maxwell or Oldroyd-B tensor models.

\\varepsilon.name: Uniaxial Strain
\\varepsilon.description: Dimensionless total mechanical deformation combining elastic and viscous contributions.

\\sigma.name: Applied Stress
\\sigma.description: Internal mechanical stress borne equally by the elastic and viscous elements.

E.name: Elastic Modulus
E.description: Instantaneous Hookean Young's modulus of the elastic spring element.

\\eta.name: Dynamic Viscosity
\\eta.description: Newtonian viscosity governing steady-state dissipative flow of the dashpot.

formulas.title: Viscoelastic Deborah Number
formulas.description: Defines the dimensionless Deborah number $\mathrm{De}$ as the ratio of a material's intrinsic stress relaxation time $\tau_r$ to the characteristic observation or deformation timescale $t_{\mathrm{obs}}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Classifies whether a viscoelastic continuum behaves predominantly as an elastic solid ($\mathrm{De} \gg 1$) or as a viscous fluid ($\mathrm{De} \ll 1$) on the timescale of a given process.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Even seemingly rigid rock flows like a liquid if you watch it for millions of years, whereas silly putty bounces like a solid if you drop it quickly.
formulas.interpretation: Non-dimensionalizing the Maxwell constitutive equation by the process timescale $t_{\mathrm{obs}}$ places $\mathrm{De} = \tau_r / t_{\mathrm{obs}} = \eta / (E t_{\mathrm{obs}})$ directly in front of the stress-rate term, controlling the crossover between viscous dissipation and elastic storage.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from Buckingham Pi dimensional scaling of temporal derivatives in viscoelastic constitutive equations.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: For $\mathrm{De} \ll 1$ the material relaxes faster than it is probed and obeys Newtonian flow; for $\mathrm{De} \gg 1$ relaxation is frozen out and Hookean elasticity dominates. Complex materials with broad relaxation spectra require defining a dominant or terminal relaxation time.

\\mathrm{De}.name: Deborah Number
\\mathrm{De}.description: Dimensionless ratio quantifying elastic versus viscous character during deformation.

\\tau_r.name: Stress Relaxation Time
\\tau_r.description: Intrinsic timescale over which internal elastic stresses decay via molecular rearrangement ($\tau_r = \eta / E$ for a Maxwell fluid).

t_{\\mathrm{obs}}.name: Observation Timescale
t_{\\mathrm{obs}}.description: Characteristic duration or inverse frequency of the applied mechanical loading.

formulas.title: Griffith Critical Fracture Stress for Brittle Solids
formulas.description: Gives the critical remote tensile stress $\sigma_f$ required for unstable brittle propagation of an internal through-thickness crack of half-length $a$ in a plane-stress elastic plate of Young's modulus $E$ and surface free energy $\gamma_s$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Establishes the thermodynamic criterion for brittle fracture by equating the elastic strain energy released per unit crack advance to the surface energy needed to create two new fracture faces.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A brittle material breaks much more easily when it contains a longer microscopic flaw, with strength falling inversely as the square root of crack length.
formulas.interpretation: For a crack of length $2a$ in a unit-thickness plate, total potential energy change is $\Delta U = -\pi a^2 \sigma^2 / E + 4 a \gamma_s$; setting $\partial \Delta U / \partial a = 0$ locates the unstable energy maximum at $\sigma_f = \sqrt{2 E \gamma_s / (\pi a)}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from global conservation of mechanical and surface free energy under virtual crack extension in a linearly elastic isotropic continuum.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Exact for an ideally brittle, linearly elastic infinite plate under plane stress with atomically sharp crack tips. In plane strain, $E$ is replaced by $E / (1 - \nu^2)$; in ductile metals, plastic dissipation $\gamma_p$ must be added to $\gamma_s$ (Irwin-Orowan modification).

\\sigma_f.name: Critical Fracture Stress
\\sigma_f.description: Minimum remote tensile stress needed to trigger catastrophic crack propagation.

E.name: Young's Modulus
E.description: Linear elastic tensile modulus of the brittle solid.

\\gamma_s.name: Specific Surface Energy
\\gamma_s.description: Thermodynamic free energy required per unit area to create a new cleavage surface.

a.name: Crack Half-Length
a.description: Half-length of an internal straight crack (or full depth of an edge crack).

formulas.title: Irwin Mode-I Crack-Tip Stress Intensity Factor
formulas.description: Quantifies the amplitude $K_I$ of the universal inverse-square-root elastic stress singularity near a mode-I opening crack tip of half-length $a$ under remote tensile stress $\sigma$ with dimensionless geometry factor $Y$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Encapsulates the combined effect of remote loading, crack size, and specimen geometry into a single local field parameter governing brittle crack stability.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Regardless of a component's overall shape, a crack grows whenever the stress intensity concentrated at its sharp tip hits a critical material toughness limit.
formulas.interpretation: Near the crack tip ($r \ll a$), opening stress scales as $\sigma_{yy}(r, \theta) = \frac{K_I}{\sqrt{2\pi r}} f_{yy}(\theta)$; equating $K_I$ to the material fracture toughness $K_{Ic} = \sqrt{E G_c}$ connects Irwin's local field criterion identically to Griffith's global energy release rate $G = K_I^2 / E$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Emerges from the biharmonic Airy stress-function eigenfunction expansion around a stress-free traction singularity under planar reflection symmetry (mode I).
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid under small-scale yielding where the plastic or nonlinear process zone at the crack tip is much smaller than crack length $a$ and specimen dimensions. Extensive ductile yielding requires elastic-plastic fracture mechanics using the $J$-integral.

K_I.name: Mode-I Stress Intensity Factor
K_I.description: Amplitude of the singular tensile opening stress field at the crack tip.

Y.name: Dimensionless Geometry Factor
Y.description: Shape correction factor accounting for finite plate width and crack configuration ($Y = 1$ for a central crack in an infinite plate).

\\sigma.name: Remote Tensile Stress
\\sigma.description: Nominal far-field tensile stress applied perpendicular to the crack plane.

a.name: Crack Half-Length
a.description: Characteristic half-length of an internal crack or length of a surface edge crack.
